title: Developing Capital Markets and Investment Fund Industries
summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers develop deep, well-regulated capital markets and fund industries through credible, well-sequenced reform.
intro: This training programme equips ministries, central banks and public agencies to develop deep, well-regulated capital markets and investment fund industries: building market infrastructure, broadening the issuer and investor base and sequencing reforms.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give the officials responsible for capital market development a practical framework for diagnosing market gaps and designing a credible reform programme. Participants leave able to identify the legal, regulatory and infrastructure prerequisites, grow the domestic issuer and investor base, develop pension and fund industries, and sequence reforms realistically.
sections.What It Covers: The role of capital markets in development, diagnosing market depth and gaps, government bond markets and the yield curve, market infrastructure, equity and corporate bond markets, the institutional investor base, pension and fund industry development, legal and regulatory prerequisites, foreign investor access, and sequencing a reform programme.
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries, treasuries and debt management offices responsible for capital market development
Central bank and public agency staff working on market development, pensions and savings policy
Staff of investment promotion agencies and financial centre bodies seeking to attract issuers, investors and fund managers
Learning Objectives: Explain how capital markets support growth and the conditions for them to develop
Diagnose the depth, liquidity and gaps of national capital markets
Assess the market infrastructure and legal and regulatory prerequisites for development
Evaluate policies to broaden the issuer base and the domestic institutional investor base
Design measures to develop pension and investment fund industries
Sequence a realistic capital market reform programme
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over two to three days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with country case studies and diagnostic exercises, ending in a reform planning workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the country's stage of market development.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial markets or economic policy is helpful. No technical background in securities or fund regulation is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
CPMI and IOSCO (2012), Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
World Bank and IMF (2001), Developing Government Bond Markets: A Handbook
OECD (2023), G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance
OECD (2016), OECD Core Principles of Private Pension Regulation

modules.title: Capital Markets and Economic Development
modules.summary: Why capital markets matter for growth, how they complement bank finance, and the economic, institutional and macroeconomic conditions that allow them to develop.
objectives: Explain the role of capital markets in financing growth
Describe how bank-based and market-based systems differ
Identify the macroeconomic and institutional preconditions for development
syllabus: Capital markets, savings mobilisation and long-term finance
Bank-based and market-based financial systems
Macroeconomic stability, rule of law and investor confidence
Case studies of capital market development paths

modules.title: Diagnosing Market Gaps and Setting Strategy
modules.summary: How to assess the depth, liquidity and structure of national markets, identify binding constraints and build a capital market development strategy with stakeholders.
objectives: Apply diagnostic indicators of market depth and liquidity
Identify binding constraints on supply, demand and infrastructure
Build governance for a capital market development strategy
syllabus: Indicators: market capitalisation, turnover, issuance and investor mix
Supply, demand and infrastructure constraints
International assessments and technical assistance
Strategy governance: ministries, regulators, exchanges and industry

modules.title: Government Bond Markets and the Yield Curve
modules.summary: Why a well-functioning government bond market is the foundation for wider capital markets, and how debt management, primary dealers and repo markets support it.
objectives: Explain the benchmark role of government securities
Assess issuance strategy, primary dealer and auction arrangements
Evaluate secondary market liquidity, repo and money markets
syllabus: Debt management strategy and benchmark issuance
Auctions, primary dealers and market makers
Repo, money markets and secondary market liquidity
Building a reliable yield curve

modules.title: Market Infrastructure: Trading, Clearing and Settlement
modules.summary: The exchanges, trading platforms, central counterparties, securities depositories and settlement systems a market needs, and the choices in ownership, governance and regulation.
objectives: Describe the main market infrastructure components and their functions
Apply the PFMI to assess infrastructure safety and efficiency
Evaluate ownership, governance and regional integration options
syllabus: Exchanges and trading venues: models and demutualisation
Central counterparties, securities depositories and settlement
The PFMI and infrastructure oversight
Regional linkages and digital market infrastructure

modules.title: Broadening the Issuer Base: Equity and Corporate Bonds
modules.summary: How to encourage companies, including mid-sized and state-owned enterprises, to raise finance through equity and corporate bond markets, and the disclosure and governance standards investors expect.
objectives: Identify the barriers that deter companies from listing or issuing bonds
Assess listing regimes, growth markets and private placement routes
Explain the corporate governance and disclosure standards investors require
syllabus: Listing requirements, costs and growth or SME markets
Corporate bonds, securitisation and private placements
State-owned enterprise listings and privatisation
Corporate governance, disclosure and minority shareholder protection

modules.title: Building the Investor Base: Pensions and Institutional Investors
modules.summary: How pension reform, insurance and other institutional investors create long-term domestic demand for capital market instruments, and the policy choices in building that investor base.
objectives: Explain how institutional investors deepen capital markets
Evaluate pension system design and investment rules
Assess the risks of directed investment and home bias requirements
syllabus: Funded pensions, mandatory and voluntary schemes
Pension governance, investment rules and the prudent person principle
Insurance, sovereign wealth and other long-term investors
Retail investors, savings incentives and financial education

modules.title: Developing an Investment Fund Industry
modules.summary: How a domestic fund industry channels savings into capital markets, the legal and regulatory foundations it needs, and the options for building local management and servicing capacity.
objectives: Describe the fund vehicles and regulatory framework a domestic industry needs
Evaluate policies to grow local fund management and servicing
Assess the role of foreign managers, cross-border funds and private markets
syllabus: Fund legislation, vehicles and fund manager and fund product rules
Depositaries, administrators and local servicing capacity
Money market funds, exchange-traded funds and private capital funds
Tax neutrality, distribution and cross-border access

modules.title: Legal Prerequisites, Foreign Access and Sequencing Reform
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining the legal and regulatory prerequisites for market development, the opening of markets to foreign investors and the realistic sequencing of reforms.
objectives: Assess the legal and regulatory prerequisites against international standards
Evaluate the benefits and risks of foreign investor access and index inclusion
Produce a sequenced capital market reform plan
syllabus: Securities law, insolvency, collateral and IOSCO principles
Capital account opening, foreign investor access and index inclusion
Sequencing reforms and avoiding common pitfalls
Workshop: a sequenced capital market development plan

related.title: Building a Competitive Financial Centre: Strategy, Regulation and Investment Promotion
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping ministries and investment promotion agencies build a competitive, reputable financial centre and measure the results.

related.title: Understanding Investment Funds for Policymakers
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving policymakers a clear grounding in how investment funds work, how they are regulated and the policy choices they raise.

related.title: AI in Financial Services: Policy Choices for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers understand AI in financial services and make informed choices on regulation, institutional roles and national strategy.

related.title: Digital Assets and Blockchain: A Policy Programme for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving policymakers the understanding to set digital asset policy, design legislation and meet international standards on crypto-assets and stablecoins.

related.title: Drafting Financial Services Legislation
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping legislative drafters and legal advisers design and draft effective, enforceable and technology-neutral financial services legislation.

related.title: Financial Crises and Public Finances: Crisis Preparedness for Government
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme preparing finance ministries and senior officials to manage financial crises, protect public finances and coordinate resolution.
